item.title: Putting a sword in SCP-447-2
item.content:encoded:
I'm surprised that this hasn't been done yet. Dr. Clef is not amused.

Date: ██/██/████
Test Subject: One katana

Procedure: The katana was submerged in SCP-447-2 for 5 minutes.

Results: The katana emerged with a distinct green tinge to the blade. Dr. Clef confiscated the katana before any tests could be conducted on its performance.

Notes: "Are you maniacs trying to give me a nervous breakdown?! The whole point of a sword is to kill people!!" - Dr. A Clef

Someone recently added 2 new entries to this experiment log and, not gonna sugar coat it, I think they are not very good. I realize this is kind of a jokey scp, but the tone of these 2 especially with the comments from the researchers come off as a little too goofy. They're missing a little bit of punctuation, which I think is what's screwing with the tone, but as well as that I think that they don't really "fit" with what's shown in the other experiment logs — it seems to me that 447 has been shown to be not a Slime What Makes Things Better (cause better is subjective), but more of a slime what makes things… like… work better at doing what they're supposed to? & I feel like its effects in the lego and passkey tests kinda aren't consistent with that vibe. For instance, maybe in the lego test, instead of it making people know how to build really good with legos, it could make the legos stick together better and be harder to break apart? Just a suggestion?

Srry for writing a whole ass novel in this wiki dot comment but I want my criticism to be constructive :-)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I think there are a few clues to what the effect of 447-2 has on dead bodies is. In this log, 447-2 did come in contact with a dead body. The SCP-882 test log. There is a dead body in there. The SCP-882 article tells us this. 2 things: 1. It was long dead and probably more dust than anything else. 2. This body was lodged between moving gears. Meaning that if 447-2's effect took place on it, brute force may be enough to fix that effect, however dangerous it may be enough to resolve it.

Also, SCP-076-2. He was repelled by its effect. So it doesn't turn them into a monster. A zombie. Or anything of the sort. Evidenced by the fact that Able likes to fight such things.

So, it can be resolved with brute force, though is not a monster… Better clues than nothing. Who else has some ideas?

item.title: Screw that 914 Test
item.content:encoded:
Look, I'm sure I'm over complicating it, but the 1:1 test with 914 really confuses me. Particually this part:

Notes: Further cross-testing of SCP-447-2 with SCP-914 has been enjoined by order of O5-██.

Now here's the problem…enjoined has 2 definitions; to instruct or urge (someone) to do something, or to prohibit someone from performing (a particular action) by issuing an injunction.

That's the problem, literally any other word could have been used, and it would have made so much more sense, but I don't know if the O5 are encouraging or prohibiting interactions with 914. Please, someone change this one word.

item.title: Mint-tinted glasses?
item.content:encoded:
I feel like the writing on this log is inconsistent and, in some places, downright sloppy. In terms of execution of concept, neither the primarily-jokey "dead bodies" thread nor the serious "what happens with dead bodies is not a thing you want to know" thread of the article feels strong enough to raise it above its dubious "no major edits/rewrites because old" status.

Honestly, every other use of 447-2 I've encountered on the wiki (not least the SCP page itself, which is awesome) has managed to hold my attention better than this, and has made the substance itself either funnier or more terrifying than even the best snippets of this log.

Admittedly I tend to have a better memory for good/compelling writing than… the alternative, so I may have forgotten an especially lazy use or two, but as a non-J, it is "too -J", and as a potential -J, it is not nearly "-J enough".

So, yeah: -1.

item.content:encoded: Think of it this way: what if, somehow, SCP-447 gets EX'd and the Foundation learns to deal with the dead bodies shtick? The gun test means that the Foundation has one more thing on their list of shit they can do with 447-2. The gun is probably gonna get melted down so it never gets used in combat, but now they know that using it in a gun works precisely as expected. Likewise, what if, for some reason, 447-2 doesn't do shit for guns besides makes them smell like mint? That's one more thing they know about it, which, in theory, puts them one step closer to EX'ing it. Quite frankly, I'm just mad that someone posted it to the log before me.
